sol.section: §12.1 K94 premises 1–2 and rejection paragraph; §3.1, §4.4, §11.1 K20; reference-interpreter/src/claims/adjoint09.rs:94–108

steps.claim: Gate angles must be finite, and K94 requires all source operand conditions of §§3–6 to hold at the claim invocation; a violated premise rejects. A classical f64 encoding may carry NaN bits, but that does not make NaN a valid rotation angle.
steps.by: clause:ISA-3.1; ISA-4.4; ISA-11.1 K20 (angle actuals reject NaN and infinities); ISA-12.1 K94 premise 2 and outcome paragraph

steps.claim: The new verifier validates f64 argument encoding and then revalidates the unbound source function. Neither operation resolves theta at its rotation use: validate_invocation09 accepts every correctly encoded f64 bit pattern, and validate_action_sequence checks only that theta has type F64.

A parsed, correctly hashed action a(x mut; theta:f64) with body rx theta x[0], empty subclaims and concrete budget [0,0,0,0] returns Ok(Proof) for theta=0x7ff0000000000000 and 0x7ff8000000000001. execute_action on those same bindings returns §4.4: rotation needs a finite angle. Finite 0 and 1 both prove and execute successfully. The parameter-uniform claim also returns Proof.

steps.claim: The oracle establishes the adjoint theorem for a concrete invocation whose required source-angle premise is false. This is an S0 proof promotion affecting certificate consumers at north-star rung 4(a).

sol.problem: severity: S0; oracle; affected rung: 4(a). Finite-angle admissibility is dropped between the concrete invocation binding and the syntactic source check. This requires no mutation of public fields: the invalid claim parses with correct hashes and verifies as Proof.
sol.fix: In §12.1 K94 state: "Resolve each rotation angle through positional classical forwarding in the checked source closure. For a concrete invocation, any nonfinite angle violates premise 2 and rejects. A parameter-uniform angle proof quantifies over source-admissible invocations satisfying §3.1 angle finiteness; it does not certify nonfinite concrete bindings. Unused f64 data arguments retain their existing encodings." Implement that binding-aware check, including reached action callees and the source bodies K94 requires checking. An alternative is an explicit finite-angle invocation-domain/guard encoding, but that changes certificate bytes; prefer the existing admissible-source precondition with explicit symbolic handling. Do not reject every parametrised rotation or globally ban NaNs as ordinary f64 data. Add NaN/infinity negatives and finite/unused-NaN/forwarded-angle positives.

sol.section: §12.1 K94 premise 2; §9.2 closure sets and §9.3 validation; reference-interpreter/src/claims/adjoint09.rs:166–246

steps.claim: K94 requires current source signature conditions and linked dependency definitions before Proof. Under §9.2 a reached oracle includes every global image in its closure, even without an explicit lift.addr reference; §9.3 requires validation. A global must define a same-name data symbol of its declared size.
steps.by: clause:ISA-12.1 K94 premise 2; ISA-9.2 "Oracle: all layout leaves ... every data image those leaves name" and "Globals are data symbols"; ISA-9.3

steps.claim: adjoint_dependencies09 collects only explicit @ operands. validate_adjoint_source09 filters data and symbols to that set, keeps layout, and does not validate its semantic data links. Consequently a global included implicitly through a reached oracle is removed before validate_symbols can check its current data signature.

The temporary witness builds an action calling a linked oracle twice with cleanup and a one-byte layout global g, without any explicit @g instruction operand. Baseline proves. Changing only g's current declared data-signature size from 1 to 2, with the byte image unchanged, still yields verify_claim=Ok(Proof) and verify_certificate=Ok(Proof). Loading the same current signature rejects with §7.2: data size differs from signature.

steps.claim: A dependency of the proved source closure escapes the current-signature premise, so the oracle again certifies too much under the public mutable Object API explicitly covered by this repair. This is S0 at north-star rung 4(a).

sol.problem: severity: S0; oracle; affected rung: 4(a). The source-closure repair covers explicit instruction references but misses layout-induced global data dependencies of reached oracles. The previous linked-function defect is repaired, but the same current-definition validity obligation remains bypassable for this data family.
sol.fix: In §12.1 K94 add: "For this premise, the dependency closure includes the data images and applicable layout dependencies selected by §9.2 for every reached definition, not only explicit instruction operands. Validate their current definitions and signatures before establishing proof." Reuse the authoritative §9.2 closure selection, or augment the traversal with all reached-oracle global-image dependencies and the corresponding current-data checks; prefer shared closure selection to a second partial graph. Preserve the deliberate exclusion of unrelated functions and the separate borrow-proof context. Add a regression for a global image present only through an oracle layout, covering invalid current signature and valid baseline.

codex.section: §12.1 K94 premise 2 and outcome rule; §4.6 loop bindings; §5.1 lifetimes; reference-interpreter/src/claims/adjoint09.rs:232-258 and src/validation.rs:172-175

steps.claim: K94 requires checking lifetime/cleanup and control premises even in zero-trip bodies, and requires rejection when a syntactic premise is violated. §4.6 requires a loop body to preserve its entry/exit live names and types; §5.1 requires each allocation to have a matching release.
steps.by: clause:ISA-12.1 K94, premise 2 and outcome paragraph; ISA-4.6 loop-binding paragraph; ISA-5.1. witness: "including nested bodies, both `qif` arms and zero-trip loop bodies"; "All source operand, signature, bounds, read-only/control, version, lifetime/cleanup and borrow conditions of §§3–6 MUST hold"; "Malformed claims, violated syntactic premises and refuted subclaims reject."

steps.claim: The new proof path delegates source discipline to validate_function. Its qloop n=0 branch validates instructions on a clone of the entry state, then discards that clone without comparing its live bindings or predicate stack with entry. Consequently opcode/operand checks run, but the loop-body exit obligations do not.
steps.by: witness: reference-interpreter/src/claims/adjoint09.rs, validate_adjoint_source09, final self.validate_function(f); reference-interpreter/src/validation.rs:172-175: if n == 0 { self.validate_action_sequence(f, &i.bodies[0], &mut s.clone())?; continue; }

steps.claim: A source-parsed perm_action @a with mut x:wire, bounds [0], no arguments, body qloop 0 { d = qalloc any 1 }, and the ordinary uniform adjoint_table claim with {} witness and [] subclaims passes parsing and check_hashes. There is no release for d, and its body exit has an additional live name. The analogous body qloop 0 { qpred x } also passes. The probe constructs and rehashes fresh source objects, rather than relying on post-parse public-field mutation.

For both malformed bodies the public claim API and whole-certificate API return Proof. The balanced allocation/release body is the positive control. Observed output: unmatched_alloc: claim=Ok(Proof); certificate=Ok(Proof) / unmatched_predicate: claim=Ok(Proof); certificate=Ok(Proof) / balanced: claim=Ok(Proof); certificate=Ok(Proof).

steps.claim: The reference oracle establishes a claim without establishing its mandatory source premises. This is S0 under the council definition even though the dynamic zero-trip operation itself is identity: the defect is certification contrary to the explicit syntactic-premise contract, not an assertion that executing zero iterations leaks a qubit. It affects certificate rung 4(a).

codex.problem: S0 (severity); oracle; north-star rung 4(a). The repair promotes malformed zero-trip sources to established/proof because its shared validator discards the body-exit state. The stated finite syntactic premises have not all been discharged. This is newly exposed by the repair issuing Proof; it is not a new parser regression.
codex.fix: Keep K94's existing requirement. In §12.1, an explicit implementation-facing sentence may say: "For a zero-trip loop, check the body's syntactic entry/exit live-name and type agreement, predicate-stack balance, and lifetime/cleanup obligations before discarding its hypothetical exit state; nonexecution does not waive these premises." Implement that check in the shared qloop validator (preferred), or add an equivalent check in adjoint_source validation. Preserve valid same-name/same-type rebinding and legal version changes; do not require identical quantum values or forbid zero-trip loops. Add claim and certificate regressions requiring rejection of qloop 0 { d = qalloc any 1 } and qloop 0 { qpred x }, with qloop 0 { d = qalloc any 1; qfree d } still proving. Merely changing these cases to Unverified would also contradict K94's rejection rule.
